Dynamic_Host_Configuration_Protocol_DHCP.objective: Clients need addresses, gateway and DNS handed out automatically.
tasks: Let's begin by configuring the DHCP_SERVER router to be a DHCP server for the 192.168.1.0 /24 subnet.  To do this, we want to create a DHCP pool of assignable addresses in the range of 192.168.1.100 - 192.168.1.199.  In order to create this pool, we need to exclude IP addresses in the ranges of 192.168.1.1 - 192.168.1.99 and 192.168.1.200 - 192.168.1.254.  DHCP_SERVER>en  DHCP_SERVER#conf t Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z. DHCP_SERVER(config)#ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.1.1 192.168.1.99 DHCP_SERVER(config)#ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.1.200 192.168.1.254

Now, we will create the DHCP pool of addresses that we want to assign, and name the pool "DEMO".  After that, set 192.168.1.1 as the IP address of the default gateway and set 8.8.8.8 as the IP address of the DNS server.  Issue all of these commands on the DHCP_SERVER router.    DHCP_SERVER(config)#ip dhcp pool DEMO DHCP_SERVER(dhcp-config)#network 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0 DHCP_SERVER(dhcp-config)#default-router 192.168.1.1 DHCP_SERVER(dhcp-config)#dns-server 8.8.8.8 DHCP_SERVER(dhcp-config)#end

On R1, let's tell our Gig 0/1 interface to get its IP address via DHCP.  Also make sure to administratively bring up interface Gig 0/1.  R1>en R1#conf t Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z. R1(config)#int gig 0/1 R1(config-if)#ip address dhcp R1(config-if)#no shutdown R1(config-if)#end

On R1, issue the "show ip int brief" command to see if we have gained an IP address via DHCP.  R1#show ip int brief Interface                  IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol GigabitEthernet0/0         unassigned      YES TFTP   administratively down down     GigabitEthernet0/1         unassigned      YES DHCP   up                    up       GigabitEthernet0/2         unassigned      YES TFTP   administratively down down     GigabitEthernet0/3         unassigned      YES TFTP   administratively down down      (##R1's discover broadcast to see if there are any dhcp servers out there will be denied because the discover broadcast cannot cross R2's router boundary.  This means that Gig 0/1 will not be assigned an IP address via DHCP.)

In order for R1 to be assigned an IP address via DHCP, we need to set R2's Gig 0/1 interface to be a DHCP Relay Agent.  R2>en R2#conf t Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z. R2(config)#int gig 0/1 R2(config-if)#ip helper-address 192.0.2.1 R2(config-if)#end

On R1, let's see if our Gig 0/1 interface has received an IP address via DHCP.  R1(config)#int gig 0/1 R1(config-if)#shutdown R1(config-if)#no shutdown R1(config-if)#end R1#show ip int brief Interface                  IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol GigabitEthernet0/0         unassigned      YES TFTP   administratively down down     GigabitEthernet0/1         192.168.1.100   YES DHCP   up                    up       GigabitEthernet0/2         unassigned      YES TFTP   administratively down down     GigabitEthernet0/3         unassigned      YES TFTP   administratively down down

Network_Time_Protocol_NTP_Lab.pdf.objective: Device clocks are out of sync, breaking logs and certs.
tasks: 1. On our INTERNET router, let's set our time to 12pm, our date to June 28, 2024, and our time zone to UTC with an offset of zero. 2. Let's set up our INTERNET router as the "ntp master" with a stratum value of 3. 3. Let's set up R1 as an "ntp server" and point it towards the 1.1.1.1 loopback interface of our INTERNET router. We are going to set up this router as if it is in the EST timezone, which would be "EST -5". 4. Let's set our R1 router to a recurring daylight savings time by using the "clock summer-time EDT recurring" command. 5. Let's verify if R1's time is synchronized with its timesource, which is our INTERNET router, by using the "show clock" command and the "show ntp status" command. 6. On R1, after the 15 minutes of waiting for R1 to fully converge with the INTERNET router, let's check our clock and NTP status and see what our time and stratum value is now. 7. On R1, let's use the "show ntp associations" command to verify that we are associated with our INTERNET router as our timesource.

steps.desc: On R1, designate which interface will be the inside NAT interface and which will be the outside NAT interface.  R1>en R1#conf t R1(config)#int gig 0/0 R1(config-if)#ip nat inside R1(config-if)#int gig 0/1 R1(config-if)#ip nat outside R1(config-if)#exit

tasks: On switch SW1, enter interface-range configuration mode for interfaces Gig 0/1-Gig 0/2, and configure IEEE 802.1Q as the trunking encapsulation for those ports.
